summary:
ARES (Astronaut Route & Exploration System) is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform designed to help future astronauts navigate the Martian surface, assess environmental risks, and conduct scientific exploration safely and efficiently.

ARES brings together NASA-derived planetary imagery, terrain information, geographic features, and environmental data within an integrated 3D Mars mapping interface. It features interactive terrain visualization, rover imagery, surface-level exploration views, and intelligent route planning using A* and Theta* pathfinding algorithms.

The platform helps mission planners identify potential obstacles, evaluate routes, explore scientific destinations, and examine environmental factors such as radiation and atmospheric conditions. By combining multiple layers of information into a single interface, ARES addresses NASA's challenge of transforming scattered planetary datasets into actionable information for human Mars exploration.

Our vision is to bridge the gap between robotic exploration data and future human missions, making Marswalk planning more informed, accessible, and efficient. ARES is a research prototype demonstrating how integrated planetary intelligence could support the next generation of explorers.

details:
ARES — Astronaut Route & Exploration System

Project Overview

ARES (Astronaut Route & Exploration System) is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform developed to support future human exploration of the Martian surface. It addresses NASA's challenge of integrating planetary datasets into a unified interface that helps astronauts plan routes, understand their surroundings, assess potential hazards, and identify scientifically valuable destinations.

How ARES Works

ARES combines NASA-derived Mars imagery, planetary geographic information, terrain data, and environmental information within an interactive mapping platform. Its key features include:

  • Interactive 3D Mars Globe: Allows users to explore Martian geography, inspect locations, and navigate planetary terrain.
  • Intelligent Route Planning: Uses A* and Theta* pathfinding algorithms to calculate efficient routes between selected locations while considering modeled terrain constraints.
  • Terrain Visualization: Provides detailed terrain representations to help users understand elevation, surface characteristics, and potential navigation difficulties.
  • Street View Exploration: Incorporates Mars rover imagery to provide a surface-level perspective of selected exploration areas.
  • Environmental Awareness: Includes experimental radiation, atmospheric, and climate-related information to support mission-planning decisions.
  • Scientific Exploration: Helps users examine geographic features and select destinations of potential scientific interest.

Technology Stack

ARES was developed using Python, FastAPI, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. The platform incorporates interactive web visualization, 3D rendering technologies, NASA-derived planetary imagery, and classical artificial intelligence search algorithms such as A* and Theta*.

The FastAPI backend handles planetary data requests, route calculations, and environmental information, while the browser-based frontend provides the interactive mission-planning experience.

Development and testing were conducted using standard computers, Git, GitHub, and Python development tools. The prototype does not require specialized astronaut hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

ARES goes beyond displaying a conventional planetary map. It combines multiple exploration functions into one interface, allowing users to move from a global view of Mars to detailed terrain inspection, route planning, and surface-level visualization.

Its innovative approach lies in connecting planetary visualization with practical exploration decisions. Rather than viewing NASA mission information as isolated datasets, ARES aims to make that information useful for planning a simulated Marswalk.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team focused on astronaut safety, terrain accessibility, route efficiency, scientific relevance, environmental awareness, usability, and the limitations of available planetary data.

We also considered the challenges of operating in an environment where direct human exploration has not yet occurred. For this reason, ARES distinguishes experimental planning capabilities from verified mission-safety information.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ARES demonstrates how information collected through decades of robotic Mars exploration could support future human missions. By bringing mapping, navigation, environmental context, and scientific exploration together, the platform aims to reduce the complexity of mission planning and improve situational awareness.

The long-term vision is to evolve ARES into a more advanced exploration assistant incorporating higher-resolution elevation models, improved hazard detection, real-time astronaut telemetry, autonomous route replanning, and offline navigation.

Ultimately, ARES represents a step toward transforming planetary science data into practical tools that could help future astronauts explore Mars more safely, efficiently, and scientifically.
